subject: Commitment criteria & routing playbook — post-call next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@clearsighthealth.com>, Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Commitment criteria & routing playbook — post-call next steps

Hi Sarah / Mike —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

1) Top pain & goals we heard
- Latency spikes impacting live triage workflows during peak hours (2–3x user-facing latency)
- Need strict tenant isolation for PHI processing and SOC-2 auditability
- Predictable run-rate: target 40M tokens / month with 10k qps burst margin

2) Proposed commitment profile (high level)
- Reserved GPU pool: 8x A100-equivalent slots (dedicated), with 2-slot burst available for 90th-percentile peaks
- Isolation: single-tenant pool + encrypted KV cache; VPC peering for egress control
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for reserved pool, P50 latency < 120ms for generation at the agreed sequence length

3) Routing / fallback playbook (to keep prod resilient)
- Primary: committed pool in us-west-2
- Fallback 1: pre-warmed pooled capacity (lower-cost variant) in us-east-1 for transient overloads
- Fallback 2: async job queue for heavy batch transforms (non-customer affecting workflows)

4) Action items & owners
- Rachel: Share commitment criteria and draft routing playbook (attached) — today (attached: CSH-Commitment-Criteria-v1.pdf, Routing-Playbook-draft.docx)
- Jordan: Ops feasibility check for burst policy and KV cache encryption — by Mon 12/07
- Mike: Share copy of procurement terms and preferred cadence for invoicing + PO timeline — by Tue 12/09
- Sarah / Procurement: Confirm any additional compliance evidence needed (SOC2 subservice, retention, audit logs) — by Wed 12/09

Attachments: CSH-Commitment-Criteria-v1.pdf; Routing-Playbook-draft.docx; SLA-Draft-v1.pdf

If that summary looks right I’ll loop in our contracts lead and send a minimal statement of work + PO checklist so procurement has a single doc to review.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Thanks Rachel — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few follow-ups from our side:

- The 8x A100 figure looks right as a starting point but can you include an estimated monthly cost range (ballpark) for the full reserved + burst profile? Procurement will need that for budget planning.
- For isolation: we need a short checklist of the audit artifacts Redwood can provide (log retention windows, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 report availability). Can you add that to the doc?
- On SLAs: is the 99.9% availability for the reserved pool compatible with our requirement for incident response within 1 hour for Sev 1? Do you have a published ETR process?

Mike and I are good with you looping in contracts; procurement will want an initial quote and a one-page SOW.

—Sarah

- Incident response / ETR: Redwood provides a 1-hour initial response for Sev1 on Dedicated customers with enterprise support (contracts addendum). The SLA-Draft-v1.pdf includes the required escalation matrix and our average historical p50/p95 recovery times for similar commitments.

- Contracts (cc) will prepare a minimal SOW + PO checklist and a draft commercial quote for 8-slot reserved pool + burst policy (ETA Wed 12/09).
- Jordan: can you confirm ops will be able to support pre-warmed burst across regions and the KV cache encryption profile before EOD Mon?

I’ll also open a HubSpot deal record and attach the three documents. Procurement / Mike / Sarah — if you confirm the budget range we’ll prioritize the 2-week procurement path.

Rachel
